title: The drive without a model
description: Owner 2026-11-08: solve the orchestrator. Design, probes and pass criterion: quality-gates-internal/plans/2026-11-08-orchestrator-without-model/PLAN.md. Prior art: plans/2026-11-05-cost-phase/analysis/prior-art-orchestrator.md.
desiredOutcome: A typed /audit:run, /audit:next or /audit:phase whose writer is a headless session runs the drive with no model request unless a step needs judgement or the human, so the orchestrator session stops being paid for relaying a script's output

tasks.title: drive-phase.py auto runs the drive's mechanical steps itself and ends with a distinct answer on done, on stop, and on a step that needs a model
tasks.description: Today the main loop is a model executing: next --signal, next --explain, run the printed run: line in background Bash, repeat (orchestrator's calls in stage-2 re-measurement k02m-k07mr, 12 to 23 per task, none carrying a decision). Add an `auto` action beside `next` in build_parser (drive-phase.py ~11769) that takes the same target forms and --task. Reuse the step result `next` builds (the signal dict in the function near 11610: step, subject, basis, next, runs, prompts) instead of parsing printed lines, and classify a step through SIGNAL_VERBS (859): done/stop end; judge/ask/review end as needs-model; dispatch with runs is executed; dispatch with no runs (an Agent) is needs-model; wait is resolved by the fact that auto itself ran the child to exit. Do not route through a shell a command the drive built, keep it an argv. wait-writer's docstring says only the main loop knows whether a session started: auto is that main loop now, so say what it knows. Exit answers are three distinct codes, documented in --help, and stdout on done/stop is what --explain prints, bounded as it is. No model is involved, so nothing here may be a new decision: every branch that the model used to take on `judge`/`ask` stays the model's or the human's. A gate's and a writer's run is a child of auto in its own process group; SIGTERM (what Esc delivers to a hook, probed 2026-11-08) is forwarded and auto exits with the stop answer, leaving the in-progress task for `next` to resume. The Bash foreground bound and gate_in_background do not apply inside auto, but leave that choice's readers intact. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A UserPromptSubmit hook runs the drive for a typed run verb and blocks the prompt only when the drive finished without needing a model
tasks.description: Probed on claude 2.1.319 (PLAN.md table): a UserPromptSubmit hook printing {"decision":"block","reason":...} ends `claude -p "/x:y"` with exit 0, total_cost_usd 0, num_turns 0, and the reason in result; a hook lived 720 s with timeout 1800 and could start a nested claude -p; interactively the CLI shows a spinner with esc to interrupt, and Esc is SIGTERM to the hook. The hook receives the prompt as typed. Docs: default timeout on this event is 30 s, so set timeout explicitly; on timeout the prompt still reaches Claude unless onFailure is "block"; reason is not added to context; hookSpecificOutput.suppressOriginalPrompt drops the "Original prompt:" tail. Hooks are importless of scripts/: resolve through hooks/_config.find_script(), launched via py-launch.sh like the others. It fires on every prompt of every session, so the prefilter for "not one of our verbs" is a string check before anything heavy, under the bench-hooks budget; SECURITY.md's fail-mode table is held by gate-parity. Fail-open here means the prompt goes on to the model and the command runs as it does today, which is safe because the drive's own lock and state decide. A new config key (default on) turns it off; adding a key is free under COMPATIBILITY.md. The command texts run.md, next.md and phase.md state the pass-through case: when the prompt reaches the model, the drive may already have advanced, so it continues with next. Check how /audit:next picks its task (audit-status READY NOW, commands/next.md) and reuse that reading rather than a second rule; if it needs a model, say why and leave that verb passing through. The run-agent-session environment scrub (PARENT_SESSION_VARS) already covers a child started from a hook; confirm rather than assume. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
